[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] CoreSite was founded in 2001 as CRG West, a Carlyle Group portfolio company, beginning operations at two West Coast carrier hotel buildings, Market Post Tower and One Wilshire, both in Los Angeles. The firm rebranded from CRG West to CoreSite in June 2009 and completed an IPO in September 2010. American Tower Corporation, the public tower and infrastructure company (NYSE: AMT, SEC CIK 1053507), completed its acquisition of CoreSite in December 2021. Stonepeak Partners LP later bought roughly 29 percent of American Towers US data center business directly in July 2022, increasing that stake to about 36 percent by October 2022. CoreSites own current Silicon Valley regional page (operator source, tier-1, https://www.coresite.com/data-center-locations/silicon-valley) names nine data centers on this Santa Clara campus, SV1 through SV9, totaling more than 1.4 million square feet campus wide, but only describes SV1, SV2, SV4, SV7, SV8, and SV9 individually, SV1 and SV2 are not rows in this registry. SV3, SV5, and SV6 are not detailed on that page, so their building specific facts below come from data center industry aggregator directories instead. CoreSites own regional page gives this specific building, SV8, an address of 3035 Stender Way, Santa Clara, CA 95054, with 161,000 plus square feet. DataCenterMap independently agrees on 3035 Stender Way. Baxtel gives a differing street number, 3045 Stender Way, for what appears to be the same building, likely a transcription difference given that both the operators own page and DataCenterMap agree on 3035, so 3035 is treated as correct here. Baxtel further describes this buildings capacity as phased, a first phase of 58,000 square feet and 6 MW critical power, growing to 18 MW at full buildout, DataCenterMap separately shows 18 MW as well. Since this is a future or phased design target rather than a confirmed single current figure from the operator, it is recorded in capacity_note only and not applied to critical_it_mw.

reading.body:
CoreSite SV8 is a 161,000+ square foot building on the Santa Clara campus of a nine-building complex totaling over 1.4 million square feet. The operator has not published a current critical power figure for this building alone. Aggregator sources describe a phased expansion from 6 MW in an initial phase to 18 MW at full buildout, but these represent design targets rather than confirmed current capacity, so the building's actual operational power draw is not known from published sources.

If SV8 reaches the stated 18 MW buildout target, that would support roughly 450 racks at 40 kW per rack, a common density for AI training infrastructure, or approximately 900 to 1,800 accelerators depending on card type. California has published capacity at 11 facilities totaling 365 MW, and Santa Clara County alone contains 103 mapped facilities. At 18 MW, SV8 would rank outside the top ten California sites by published capacity but would represent meaningful density within Silicon Valley's infrastructure footprint.

The building's status as a disclosed phase of a larger campus, combined with the absence of a current operator-confirmed power specification, means SV8's relevance to near-term AI scaling depends on whether and when the full buildout is realized. The facility is accessible to assessment only through third-party aggregator data until the operator publishes a current capacity figure.
